_comment: Hand-written plugins.json for checks.dev-plugins: basic-config's lock plus a non-empty
localPlugins, which no other fixture has.
make-env reads only the *keys* of localPlugins; every one of them routes to <devPath>/<name>,
and the value is never looked at. The two entries pin that from both sides:
dirred.nvim has a `dir`, deliberately pointing somewhere devPath would never produce, so the
check fails loudly if anyone starts reading it. It is ignored not for being machine-specific
-- back when a lock still recorded a dir, one the spec wrote absolute came through unchanged
-- but because a spec-level dir short-circuits lazy before dev.path is ever consulted
(lua/lazy/core/meta.lua:214-217), so reading it could not change any resolved directory.
Since #56, resolve.lua records no dir for any local plugin, so no real lock can produce this
shape any more; what is here stands for the *shape* of a plugins.json committed before #56,
which make-env still has to tolerate -- the value itself is kept unrealistic on purpose (see
the last paragraph). checks.dev-plugins' dirredRecordedDir binding is what keeps this value
from being tidied into null or into devPath's own answer -- either edit would make the
assertion above pass for the wrong reason (nothing left to ignore, or an answer that matches
ignoring it anyway).
bare.nvim has no `dir` at all, so make-env must not need one. This shape used to be hand-made
only: extract.lua dumped `dir = p.dev and p.dir or nil`, and lua/lazy/core/meta.lua:229-238
always filled a dev plugin's dir in (measured: a bare `dev = true` came out
{"dev":true,"dir":"<HOME>/projects/..."}), so no lock could ever emit a dev entry missing
`dir`. #47's local_dir can return nil for a `dev = true` plugin whose own dev.path happens to
point back under lazy's own root -- a pathological config, see the plan's SS7 -- and
resolve.lua's `p.dev or p.dir` then falls back to `dev` alone, so a real lock could already
write exactly this shape too before #56. Since #56, this is not just that pathological case's
shape any more -- it is the shape every entry in a real lock has, regardless of how the
plugin became local (#47), because resolve.lua writes an empty object for all of them. It
stands for the pathological-dev.path case, for a plugins.json written by an older or future
resolve.lua that omits the key outright, and now for every entry a real lock writes, and it
is what makes `v.dir` reintroduced without an `or` fallback fail here rather than in a
user's config.
dirred.nvim's literal `~` could not have come out of any real lock, pre-#56 ones included:
Util.norm expands `~` before extract.lua ever sees it. It is kept because it contrasts so
visibly with devPath.
